agent_note: Third-person retrospective thriller centred on Maya, a veteran. 21 event quotes, all past, including unfakeable concrete narration ("She made sure the Glock was loaded and closed the safe"). The distinctive feature is a very heavy essayistic 2nd-person-present layer: 16 of 49 quotes are gnomic, mostly "you"-universals about war, marriage, and parenting. A two-bucket filter would read most of those as present-tense evidence and could flip this book to present - this is the single biggest risk in the set, and it is distributed across many quotes rather than one. Several quotes mix a past narrative clause with a present universal (q01318, q01319, q01341, q01356); those were bucketed by which move dominates and are noted individually.
